sections.html:
Oak Ridge is a planned town, built in 1942 about 25 miles east of Knoxville, and many of its early houses went up fast from cemesto panels, which are bonded cement and asbestos. An inspector or buyer may ask about the original construction of an older house here, so know when yours was built.

Mid-2025 estimates give the city 35,395 residents, up 12.7% since 2020. Homes their owners live in have a median value of $270,200, and 65.8% of homes fit that description. Renters pay a median $1,131. People 65 and over make up 19.6% of the city, so a good share of listings come from downsizing and estate sales.

Oak Ridge sends two bills. The city mails its own statement in July and collects it at the Utilities Business Office, 200 South Tulane Avenue. The county portion is billed by Anderson or Roane County, depending on where the parcel lies. About 16.25% of taxable real parcels are in the Roane County section.

Oak Ridge tax rates per $100 of assessed value
Section of Oak RidgeCity rateCounty rateTotal
Anderson County (tax year 2023)$2.3136$2.456$4.7696

Houses are assessed at a quarter of appraised value. For this year's exact rate, call the Utilities Business Office at (865) 425-3400.

The city allows payment without interest until August 31, and interest begins September 1. You can pay online, at the Utilities Business Office, in the lot drop box, or by mailing a check to P.O. Box 1, Oak Ridge, TN 37831. Card payments carry a 2.75% fee, and eChecks cost $1 for each $5,000.

Statements go to the owner address the state held on January 1. After a spring or summer sale, the new owner may never get one, and closing normally covers that gap. A missing notice never erases the debt. The city bill falls due in summer and the county bill in the fall, so a seller closing between the two should have the title company pull both.

Properties in both the Anderson and Roane sections were reappraised in fiscal years 2016 and 2021, tied to tax years 2015 and 2020. The city rate fell from $2.56 in the 2019 tax year to $2.3136 after the second reappraisal, a drop of about 10%. The Anderson County rate fell from $2.6945 to $2.456.

State law fixes assessment ratios at 25% for residential property, 40% for commercial and 30% for personal equipment. The city does not set appraised values. If you disagree with yours, ask the Anderson or Roane County assessor how to request a review.

Tennessee's freeze and relief programs run through the counties. The Comptroller's 2026 list puts the freeze income ceiling at $53,900 in Anderson County and $43,460 in Roane County, and applications close 35 days after the local delinquency date.

If you already benefit from one, say so before closing so the settlement figures match the bill that is really owed.

Call Codes Enforcement at 865-425-3532 for building permits. The division also polices housing, plumbing, electrical and zoning rules, and permit work now runs through the CityView portal. A three-day appeal form exists for housing code violations, and it must be returned in person within three days of signing for a certified notice.

  • A vacant building must keep its doors and windows locked or otherwise secured.
  • Every house must show its number at the front entrance or on the mailbox.
  • A structure tax-delinquent for three years can be treated as deteriorated under the rental inspection chapter.

Chapter 5 of Title 13 allows residential rental inspection districts. A landlord selling a rental should ask Planning and Development whether the address is in one.

sections.h2: Recording a deed in Anderson or Roane County
sections.html:
A deed is recorded in the county where the land lies. In Anderson County that is the Register of Deeds in Clinton, 100 North Main Street, Room 205, open weekdays 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Its indexes are online with no user fees, and a buyer can look up your records there. The state adds a 37-cent levy per $100 of sale price.

Check which county holds your parcel before you order a title search. Anderson and Roane keep separate records and tax maps. Most sellers leave the search and filing to the title company.

Many Oak Ridge homes sit on the steep northeastern slope of Blackoak Ridge, and the east-side lakefront has trails and picnic areas. Lot shape and slope matter more here than on a flat grid. Gutters, drainage and air conditioning are routine inspection items, so expect questions about them from any buyer who walks the lot.

• The July city statement and any county statement for the fall, whichever county holds your parcel.
  • Your deed, with the parcel's county confirmed on the tax map.
  • Permit records from Codes Enforcement for any repairs.
  • Proof of enrollment, if you receive a freeze or relief benefit.
  • Lease details, if a tenant lives in the house.

Older cemesto houses deserve one extra step: write down what you know about the original construction and any remodeling, so you can answer a buyer's questions without guessing.

sections.h2: If taxes are owed when you sell
sections.html:
Because interest begins September 1, a sale in the fall can leave a city balance already accruing. The title company asks the Utilities Business Office for the city figure and the county for its share, then pays both from your proceeds. You do not need to bring cash to the table, but you do need accurate numbers early, so ask for them when you accept an offer.

A buyer should not be left to find a missing statement later. Since a lost notice never erases the debt, settle the year in writing before the deed is signed.

An agent listing suits a tidy house whose owner can wait on a buyer's loan. Cash offers tend to fit houses that need work, inherited houses and rentals with tenants, and closing then depends on clear title and lien payoffs.

With a cash sale there is no lender, so no bank appraisal or loan approval holds up the date, and you can plan the move around a closing you can count on. Whatever the buyer, put the offer in writing, settle who pays the recording tax and let the title company verify the city and county tax status.

faqs.q: When does Oak Ridge city property tax become delinquent?
faqs.a: Interest starts September 1. Statements arrive in July, and August 31 is the last day to pay without it.

faqs.q: Which county handles my Oak Ridge deed?
faqs.a: Whichever county holds the parcel. Anderson holds most of the city, and about 16.25% of taxable real parcels sit in Roane County, so check your tax map first.

faqs.q: What is the Oak Ridge city tax rate?
faqs.a: The city rate is $2.3136 per $100 assessed through the last year in its rate table. The Utilities Business Office, (865) 425-3400, can tell you the rate on this year's bill.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to repair a house before selling it?
faqs.a: For building work, yes. Codes Enforcement issues every building permit, and trade permits go to applicants with valid city or state licenses. The number is 865-425-3532.

faqs.q: Can a buyer see my county records online?
faqs.a: Yes for Anderson County. Its Register of Deeds offers online access to indexes and images and has removed user fees.
